description.en-US: The human reference for this agreement, unique within its organization. Immutable: it is quoted to the vendor and cited on every order drawn against it, so changing it would strand those references.
The vendor's own reference for the agreement, if they gave one.

A blanket order commits to quantities at agreed prices and tracks what has been drawn down; a purchase template is a reusable skeleton with no commitment. Immutable because the two are tracked differently and switching types would make the ordered quantities of the first meaningless (BR 32).

The business lifecycle. Written only by the confirm, close and cancel actions, never by a plain update, so that no transition can happen without its audit event (BR 33, PUR-R3, PUR-R6). Independent of is_archived: a closed agreement may be archived or not, and both combinations are meaningful (BR 34).

The supplier this agreement is with. Optional by type: a blanket order names one, a purchase template need not. A plain ulid with no edge — the party belongs to Contacts, and a foreign key across a module boundary would make Purchase's schema depend on Contacts' table. Validated through a port, which also checks the party has a vendor profile.
The purchaser responsible. A plain ulid: the user belongs to IAM.
What the agreed prices are denominated in. A plain ulid: the currency belongs to Essential. There is no exchange-rate model, so one agreement is in one currency and its prices are never converted.
When the agreement stops being drawable against. Not enforced by the schema — an expired agreement stays readable, and refusing a late order is the confirm action's decision, not a column's.
